faq: What does this tool calculate?
Decimal degrees multiplied by 60 to give arcminutes, with whole-degree separation where the degrees-minutes form is wanted.
Is the calculation done locally?
Yes — instant, in the browser.
How accurate is the result?
Definitional — 60′ per degree exactly. The input's accuracy is the output's ceiling.
Which datum do these coordinate tools use?
Unit conversion is datum-blind; the values it serves on this site are WGS84.
Do more decimal places always mean better accuracy?
Minutes to three decimals (0.001′ ≈ 1.9 m of latitude) already out-resolve most sources. Beyond that, costume.
Full coordinates at once?
The Coordinate Converter dresses whole pairs in degrees-minutes directly; this page is the single-value lane.
Arcminutes of longitude?
Same ×60 arithmetic — but remember a longitude arcminute's ground size shrinks with latitude, priced by the Arcseconds family tools.
Negative values?
Signs carry through — western and southern conversions stay honest.
Seconds too?
Split the minutes' fraction ×60 again for arcseconds, or use the DMS converters for the full dress in one step.
Why 60?
Babylonian sexagesimal, inherited through astronomy into navigation — the oldest unit system you will use today.
Rounding drift on round trips?
Convert, convert back: float arithmetic returns your value to display precision. Any visible drift is a display-rounding choice, correctable in the precision tools.
